title: IC Substrate Inspection - Residue Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Post-Implant Quality Validation for 22nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Priya Sharma

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify Residue defects during post-implant inspection at the 22nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab A to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Residue defects that are critical to yield at the 22nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: IC Substrate Inspection
- Target Defect: Residue
- Process Step: Post-Implant
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 22nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab A

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab A for post-implant monitoring in the 22nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v15.0.632
Recipe: IC_SUBSTRATE_INSPECTION_22nm_POST_IMPLANT
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: High (114 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'IC Substrate Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Residue defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 22nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 84 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 93% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.7% for IC Substrate Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-05-21
Wafers Tested: 11
Total Defects Found: 2112
Defect Density: 298.79 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.0%
Capture Rate: 90.1%
Test Duration: 344 minutes
System Uptime: 98.2%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Residue at the 22nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) SECS/GEM communication was verified with zero packet loss during data transfer.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Residue at 22nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
